explanations.explanation: You got it, baker! Paul just said Christ set them free, so now he tells them, "Stand firm, then…" (Galatians 5:1). You don't wander off from a gift like that. That's like me getting called out of a dark junk drawer and then hopping my gold base right back inside to take a nap under the old takeout menus.

explanations.answer: Work hard to earn their freedom
explanations.explanation: Hold on, friend, they don't have to earn what they already have! Paul starts by saying, "It is for freedom that Christ has set us free" (Galatians 5:1). Since Christ already did the freeing, Paul tells them to stand firm in it. Trying to buy a cookie box that somebody already paid for and handed to you is just doing extra math for no reason.

Paul isn't telling anybody to hush up here. He says Christ has set us free, and then he commands them, "Stand firm, then…" (Galatians 5:1). He wants them planted right where Christ put them, not hiding in the corner like a shy cookie stamper behind the flour canister.

Spot on, friend. Right after telling them to stand firm, Paul says, "and do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery" (Galatians 5:1). A yoke is a heavy wooden beam you put on oxen to make them pull a load. Why would anyone trade freedom for a heavy wooden neck brace?

That warning is right there in the verse, baker! Paul tells them, "Stand firm, then, and do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery" (Galatians 5:1). Christ already set them free, and Paul doesn't want them strapping that heavy load back on.

Paul does not soften that one bit, does he? He writes, "if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no value to you at all" (Galatians 5:2). He wants them to see how serious this choice really is.

It's the exact opposite, baker. Paul isn't treating circumcision like a nice sprinkle you add on top to make things better. He warns them that if they let themselves be circumcised, "Christ will be of no value to you at all" (Galatians 5:2).

Oh, it doesn't stay the same at all, friend. Paul says, "if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no value to you at all" (Galatians 5:2). That is a massive warning, and Paul puts his own name right at the front of the verse so nobody misses it.

Not just that one command, baker! Paul testifies to every man who gets himself circumcised "that he is obligated to obey the whole law" (Galatians 5:3). You don't get to pick one rule off the tray like a single chocolate chip and leave the rest behind. If you sign up for that path, you're on the hook for the whole thing.

You read it right, friend. Paul says, "Again I testify to every man who gets himself circumcised that he is obligated to obey the whole law" (Galatians 5:3). There is no one-command deal here. It's the whole law, top to bottom.

explanations.answer: They have been severed from Christ
explanations.explanation: That is a heavy word, baker, and it's the exact one Paul uses. He writes, "You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ; you have fallen away from grace" (Galatians 5:4). Trying to be made right by the law cuts a person off from the very One who sets us free.

explanations.answer: They have drawn closer to Christ
explanations.explanation: I think the folks pushing the law probably thought it sounded religious, but Paul says the exact opposite. He writes, "You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ…" (Galatians 5:4). Instead of bringing them closer, it cuts them off from Christ and means they have fallen away from grace.

Friend, grace and earning don't mix like that here. Paul tells those trying to be justified by the law that they "have been severed from Christ; you have fallen away from grace" (Galatians 5:4). Instead of getting extra grace, they fall away from it.

Yes indeed, baker! Right after talking about those trying to be justified by the law, Paul shows the true way: "But by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness" (Galatians 5:5). It's by faith and through the Spirit, not by strapping that yoke back on.

Careful there, friend, the law is what verse 4 just warned against! In verse 5, Paul turns the corner and says, "But by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness" (Galatians 5:4-5). It's faith, not law, that goes in that blank.

Paul isn't bragging on human hustle here, baker. He says, "But by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness" (Galatians 5:5). We wait eagerly by faith through the Spirit, not by flexing our own muscles.

That is the line to put on the front of the bakery right there! Paul says neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value in Christ Jesus, and then he tells us what counts: "What matters is faith expressing itself through love" (Galatians 5:6). Faith isn't sitting quietly in the back of a drawer. It shows up through love.

Paul just spent the last five verses warning them away from trying to be justified by the law (Galatians 5:1-5). In Christ Jesus, he says, "What matters is faith expressing itself through love" (Galatians 5:6). That's what has real value.

explanations.answer: Coming from the right family line
explanations.explanation: Paul doesn't bring up family trees here, friend. He wipes away the divide over circumcision and says, "For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value. What matters is faith expressing itself through love" (Galatians 5:6). That's the whole heartbeat of it.

Whoa now, don't pin that roadblock on God! After asking who obstructed them from obeying the truth, Paul says flat out, "Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you" (Galatians 5:7-8). Whoever is talking them into this, it is NOT the One who called them.

You caught it, baker. Paul makes sure they know the source: "Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you" (Galatians 5:8). They were running well, and the voice trying to trip them up is definitely not the One who called them.

Every last bit of it, baker! Paul says, "A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (Galatians 5:9). You don't put a pinch of leaven in a bowl and expect it to stay polite in one corner. Give it a little time and the whole bowl is rising!

Leaven doesn't stop at the top like sprinkles on a sugar cookie, friend. Paul says, "A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (Galatians 5:9). Even a tiny bit spreads all the way through everything in the bowl.

If dough worked like that, baking would be a very strange business! Paul reminds them how baking really works: "A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (Galatians 5:9). A little bit of this persuasion doesn't stay in one spot; it works through the whole batch.

You nailed it, friend. Paul writes, "The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be" (Galatians 5:10). It doesn't matter how big a name that troublemaker has. He is going to answer for stirring up the church.

explanations.answer: He will be let off free
explanations.explanation: Nobody is getting a free pass for messing with the believers here. Paul says, "The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be" (Galatians 5:10). Paul is confident the Galatians will come through, and the troublemaker will face judgment.

explanations.answer: He will be put in charge
explanations.explanation: Oh, he is definitely not getting a promotion, baker! Paul says, "The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be" (Galatians 5:10). Stirring up the churches of Galatia leads to judgment, not the boss's chair.

Look closer at how he asks it, friend: "Now, brothers, if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted?" (Galatians 5:11). He is using that question to show he is NOT preaching it! If he were preaching circumcision, people wouldn't be persecuting him for his message about the cross.

Right you are, baker! Paul asks, "if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted?" (Galatians 5:11). The whole point of his question is that he is NOT preaching circumcision, and the persecution he's facing proves it.

You got it, friend. Paul tells them, "For you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh" (Galatians 5:13). Freedom in Christ isn't a green light to act selfishly. It's freedom to love and serve one another.

He really does give them that warning, baker! Paul writes, "For you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh" (Galatians 5:13). He wants them to stand firm in freedom, and he also makes sure they don't twist that freedom into an excuse for the flesh.

Look at that, baker! All those arguments about the law, and Paul says, "The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: 'Love your neighbor as yourself'" (Galatians 5:14). That matches right up with what he said back in verse 6 about faith expressing itself through love, and what he just said in verse 13 about serving one another in love.

Remembering the Sabbath day is one of the Ten Commandments back in Exodus 20:8, friend, not the single decree Paul names here. In Galatians 5:14, Paul writes, "The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: 'Love your neighbor as yourself.'" It all comes down to love.

Honoring your father and mother is a famous command from Exodus 20:12, baker, and Paul even quotes it in Ephesians 6:2. Here in Galatians 5:14, though, the single decree he gives is, "Love your neighbor as yourself." That's the one that fulfills the entire law.

You nailed it, friend. Paul writes, "But if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out, or you will be consumed by one another" (Galatians 5:15). Biting and devouring are for cookies, baker, NEVER for the people sitting around the table with you!

Listen to the words Paul uses at the start of the verse: "biting and devouring" (Galatians 5:15). He finishes that same picture by warning, "watch out, or you will be consumed by one another" (Galatians 5:15). If people keep taking bites out of each other, there won't be anybody left!

Paul goes way past embarrassment with this warning, baker. Because he starts with "biting and devouring one another," he warns that they will be "consumed by one another" (Galatians 5:15). Instead of serving each other in love, they'd end up swallowing each other whole.
